text:
tanvi: heads up — noticed a p99 uptick in streaming under the new kernel selector change when microbatch size == 4. low-volume repro on canary.

darren: ugh. observed that too on the east region canary. p50/p95 fine, p99 jumped ~120ms. seems correlated with small emit windows.

olga: any KV-cache misses in the traces? small microbatches often force cache rehydration on replica handoff.

ashwin: i looked at the flame graphs. seems like the quantized-attn path hits a slow memmove when flushing partial KV pages mid-request. attaching snippet from a single 1k-token session:

perf-bot: profiling run finished: https://redwood.internal/perf/streams/2068 (summary below)

perf-bot: 
```
summary: sample=2000 requests
p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=190ms
config: microbatch=4, emit_interval=12ms, kernel_policy=v1 (select by seq_len)
notes: tail spikes align with KV page writes and repeated kernel handoff between fused and fallback kernels
```

tanvi: interesting. so kernel handoffs + small emit intervals => more page thrash. that explains perceived stutter.

darren: hypothesis: increase per-stream emit interval from 12ms -> 24ms for microbatch 4, or prefer a single kernel binding for duration of a stream to avoid handoffs. either could reduce p99 at cost of a little throughput.

olga: can we try a loveseat approach: keep emit interval small for low-latency short responses, but for long streams detect repeated kernel switches and force 'sticky-kernel' for that session. i can prototype sticky-kernel flag in runtime.

ashwin: +1. also we should try changing microbatching heuristic: for models with dense KV (long context) prefer microbatch >=8, otherwise set to 2-4. current heuristic always tries to keep microbatch small which hurts tail for long-context workloads.

tanvi: can we get a quick A/B? 1) sticky-kernel + emit=12ms; 2) sticky-kernel + emit=24ms; 3) no-sticky + emit=24ms + microbatch=8. want p50/p95/p99 and throughput QPS baseline.

perf-bot: queued experiments: ab-test-id=st-kernel-2068, variants: A,B,C. will run 5k streams each.

darren: for telemetry, add these metrics to the run: kernel-switch-count, kv-page-writes, avg-emit-chunk-size, per-stream-first-byte-latency.

olga: note: kernel-switch-count should be cheap to increment — avoid atomic contended ops on hot path. we can sample 1% and extrapolate.

ashwin: also instrument 'perceived-latency' as first-byte intervals over the first N tokens (8 tokens). that's what product cares about.

tanvi: thanks team. if AB looks good, we'll roll to canary and watch p99 for 24h. i expect tradeoff: variant B reduces p99 ~80-120ms but might drop aggregate throughput 3-6%. is acceptable for SLOs.

darren: ping me when perf-bot finishes, i'll pull raw traces and run the trace-diff script: `tools/trace-diff --left A --right C --focus=kv,kernel`

perf-bot: AB runs complete. quick numbers (A/B/C):

perf-bot: 
```
A: p50=19ms p95=70ms p99=185ms qps=980
B: p50=21ms p95=68ms p99=110ms qps=940
C: p50=24ms p95=90ms p99=130ms qps=1020
```

olga: Variant B looks promising for tail. qps hit isn't massive and p99 halved vs A.

ashwin: trace-diff shows kernel-switches per-stream: A=3.1, B=0.4, C=3.0. KV-page-writes sampled: A=1.6, B=0.5, C=1.5. sticky-kernel clearly reduced thrash.

tanvi: ok let's roll sticky-kernel + emit=24ms only for long-context models (seq_len>2k) and keep default for short responses. create rollout ticket and canary window.

darren: created rollout ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-4872 — assigning to eng-runtime for staged rollout.

olga: follow-up: we should add a kernel-selection cost-estimate step in the planner to avoid oscillations when latency and throughput signals conflict. open a small RFC?

tanvi: please do. thanks everyone. :rocket:
